answer: Every agent anchors its identity to a juniper registry entry that records a plume of completed, publicly verifiable jobs. A new identity must lock a refundable bond that only unlocks after twenty epochs of honest work, and the plume history is non-transferable, so a Sybil farmer cannot copy it. If peers challenge a job and the work fails verification, the bond is slashed and the anchor is burned. Creating a thousand fakes thus costs a thousand bonds plus twenty epochs of real work each, while one honest agent pays once.
